text:
maya: Customer escalation — end user got a promo applied instead of a refund. Raised because order was charged but refund failed and promo code appeared on account. Urgent, customer angry :(

eli: Can you paste the request that hit the autorouter + any logs we have?

maya: Pasting minimal reproduction from our support UI logs: 
```json
POST /v1/actions/dispatch
{
  "user_id": "acct_9z",
  "nlp_result": "I want a refund for order 12345",
  "tools_candidates": [
    {"name": "apply_promo", "sig": "(account_id, code)"},
    {"name": "issue_refund", "sig": "(account_id, amount, reason)"}
  ]
}
```
logs show the router chose `apply_promo` and returned 200 after writing a promo token to the account. No refund record created.

samir: That request shape looks ambiguous to the selector — the NL text mentions "refund" but our selector weights are heavily influenced by short signature match and recent usage. `apply_promo` signature is shorter so it wins in tie-breaker heuristics.

ops-bot: autorouter event: route_decision={chosen:apply_promo, score:0.62, reason:"sig_similarity"}  at 2026-05-02T14:03:20Z

eli: Repro steps I used locally (works):
1) curl -s -X POST https://router.internal/v1/route -d '{"text":"I need a refund","context":{}}'
2) see chosen tool `apply_promo` in response.

maya: Customer support expectation: when user explicitly says refund/refunded/return, router should favor refund tools. This is a regression from last month.

samir: Quick investigation note — both tools were onboarded with overlapping param names. Example: `apply_promo(account_id, code)` vs `issue_refund(account_id, amount, reason)` but our selector ignores token-level intent when signatures overlap.

eli: Proposed short-term fix: add a token-trigger rule that boosts any tool with name containing "refund" when the NL includes refund-related lemmas (refund, returned, credit). Can we toggle that today behind a flag?

samir: Yes, we can push a routing-policy patch. Plan:
- create feature-flag `boost_refund_intent` (config)
- default off, enable for 10% canary on support orgs
- monitor false positives for 48h

maya: Also we need customer remediation: issue the refund manually and apologize. I've queued a manual refund and sent an email.

eli: For root cause we should also do a long-term fix: train selector with labels for these ambiguous pairs and incorporate explicit intent classifier output into routing score.

maya: For reproducer to SRE/Runtime: payload snippet that causes misroute attached above. TL;DR: ambiguous NL + overlapping tools => wrong tool.

samir: I'll open a PR with the flag + test + rollout playbook. cc @maya to validate canary.

maya: Thanks — please include a rollback step. Also adding an assertion in support UI that shows predicted tool to agents so they can catch misroutes earlier :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rollout:created {flag:boost_refund_intent, scope:support-orgs, pct:10}

eli: Monitoring checklist: watch for increased apply_promo invocations, drop in refund-requests resolved on first touch, and customer reopens. I'll add dashboards.

maya: Closing loop — customer refunded manually, will follow up if they see anything else.

samir: Will update thread with PR link and canary results in 2 hours.

maya: :white_check_mark:
